purpose: Single machine authority for the optional cross-plan continuity artifact: what a completed plan may leave behind, where it is stored, who writes it, who reads it, and what it deliberately does not do. Continuity is optional and never sticky. It is not a history store, a conversation log, an activity journal, or a second archive; it does not replace archive/PLAN-NNN/ and it does not make archival mandatory.
vocabulary_rule: Every label, state, and code below is domain-neutral. Outcome, evidence, decision, risk, delivery, and follow-up are the concepts; software, policy, research, and operations examples may illustrate a row but never define one.

storage.authority: There is exactly one per project. A file of that name anywhere else — inside resources/, inside archive/PLAN-NNN/, in a work root, in a subdirectory — is not continuity: no reader resolves it and no writer produces it.
storage.reset_rule: reset-plan operates on a closed, code-owned allowlist that does not name CONTINUITY.md, and archive/ is not a reset target. The allowlist must never be extended to remove it.
storage.archive_rule: ARCHIVE_ROOT_FILES must never gain CONTINUITY.md. A per-plan copy would go stale at the next closeout and would force a reader to choose between two authorities.

activation.question: How should this completed plan be preserved — (1) not at all; (2) full archive only; (3) full archive plus a compact continuity index; or (4) a compact continuity ledger only, without a full archive?
activation.asked: identically at every closeout, replacing the archive question rather than sitting beside it

outcomes.meaning: No preservation. Reset intentionally discards this plan's history and decisions.
Full archive only. Today's behavior, unchanged.

Full archive plus a compact continuity index. Offered only as an extension of outcome 2; its rows locate decision bodies inside archive/PLAN-NNN/decisions/, so it cannot be selected without the archive.

A compact continuity ledger instead of a full archive. The only outcome that preserves rulings without an archive: because no bodies survive, its rows carry no locator and the ruling text is the entire surviving record.

activation.disabled_path_guarantee: A none or archive closeout performs zero continuity reads and zero continuity writes, unconditionally — in every project state, including one that already carries a CONTINUITY.md and including one whose artifact is damaged. This covers the whole transition, not only its last two commands: the bounded release that may precede a disabled closeout after a failed ledger attempt reads and writes no continuity content either.
activation.startup_guarantee: Startup and status cost zero continuity bytes only where no root CONTINUITY.md exists. A prior enabled artifact stays projectable until an enabled-path operation changes it or the operator removes it; a disabled closeout neither reads nor revokes it.

identity.rationale: DEC-NNN is allocated per plan and demonstrably reused across plans, so a cross-plan set keyed on it would be ambiguous the first time a second plan recorded a row. The contract adds no new numbering scheme; it qualifies the existing one.

reference_grammar.bare_meaning: a decision in the plan window now closing — the current decisions/ directory
reference_grammar.qualified_meaning: a decision recorded in a closed plan window; the only form that can reach a live row from a prior plan

body_locator.validated: once, at the write that creates the row, and never again

schema.section_order_rule: Load-bearing. A reader composing the startup projection stops at the ## Cold index heading, so startup parse cost is bounded by the header, the live table, and one cold counter line and does not grow as cold rows or closed plans accumulate.
schema.cold_counters: - Superseded: <n>; Expired: <n>; Pruned: <n>; Retrieval: <body | ruling | mixed | none>
schema.removed_by_meaning: The column records who ended the rule, not what replaced it: under pure expiry it names an id that has no live row and never will.
schema.ledger_heading_rule: The preservation value is composed by the writer from the invocation's --mode at the compute pass that first records the plan, never authored by the PM. Once written it is immutable: a later ledger-replace carries the whole heading through byte for byte and refuses a --mode or --closed that disagrees.

field_groups.label: Outcome
field_groups.preserves: intended outcome, terminal state, and a verification value
field_groups.excludes: a narrative work log or any conversation

field_groups.label: Evidence
field_groups.preserves: a compact reference to the decisive observation and its state
field_groups.excludes: raw evidence bodies copied into the ledger

field_groups.label: Decisions
field_groups.preserves: counts of governing, superseded, and expired decisions as of that plan's closeout

field_groups.label: Risks
field_groups.preserves: material unresolved risk, its disposition, and its trigger and owner when follow-up exists

field_groups.label: Delivery
field_groups.preserves: deliverable identity, target, and delivery/acceptance state

field_groups.label: Follow-up
field_groups.preserves: remaining action, owner, condition, and open/closed state
field_groups.excludes: a plan for the next cycle

schema.gaps: Plans recorded counts ### PLAN-NNN sections, not plan ids. A missing id between two recorded ids means exactly one thing: that plan closed with outcome 1 or 2, so nothing about it was preserved here. It never means data loss, and it is distinguishable from a pruned entry, which remains present as a tombstone.

decision_headers.source: The decision file body is the single authoritative source for Scope, Ruling, Status, Supersedes, and Expires. write-continuity reads those headers and never invents, derives, or infers them.
decision_headers.write_decision_rule: write-decision gains no new flags and renders no header. It gains a fail-closed validation pass over the body it was handed: any Scope, Ruling, Supersedes, or Expires header present must satisfy the field and reference grammars, or the write is refused with usage and exit 2 before a byte lands.
decision_headers.index_rule: decisions/INDEX.md stays a human index. It is not a continuity input, gains no column, and is never consulted by write-continuity.

rules: non-empty after stripping leading and trailing spaces
no CR (U+000D), no LF (U+000A), and no C0 or C1 control character
valid UTF-8 with no unpaired surrogate
within both the character and the serialized-byte bound
field_grammar.escaping: refused, never escaped: the value must be byte-identical in the Markdown cell and in the JSON projection, or the declared byte bound means two different things
field_grammar.serialized_bytes_definition: the UTF-8 byte length of the value after JSON string escaping, excluding the surrounding quotes — exactly the bytes it contributes to the record cli.emit.emit_record writes

enforcement_points.over: the headers present in the authored body

bounds.rule: Every value here is an engineering bound derived from the accepted contract's measurements, not an operator-reserved choice. A value that would exceed a bound is a fail-closed refusal naming the field and the bound it broke, never a silent truncation.

projection.condition: if and only if the root CONTINUITY.md exists and satisfies every read-contract condition. When the artifact is absent the key is absent from the record; "continuity":null is never serialized. When the artifact is present and defective no record is emitted at all.
projection.row_selection: reverse recording order — most recently recorded first — while both of at most 4 rows and the serialized bound hold. Rows that do not fit are omitted, truncated is set, and the omitted count appears in live_omitted. A projection is never emitted over the bound and a row is never dropped without saying so.
projection.rendered_body_rule: compose-state's rendered_body — the text that becomes STATE.md — gains no continuity section. Continuity reaches the session through the machine record, not through the state file.
projection.retrieval_derivation: body if every live and cold row carries a locator; ruling if none does; mixed if some do and some do not; none if there are no live or cold rows at all. It is a derived summary over the rows actually present, never a mode.

read_contract.rule: Absence is a successful disabled record. Presence with any defect is a fail-closed refusal — for the readers that read it, and for nothing else.

states.readers: exit 0; record emitted; continuity key absent

states.state: present, regular, st_nlink == 1, valid UTF-8, Format: continuity-v1, all five sections parse
a required section or field malformed

read_contract.no_degradation: A defective artifact that silently produced a record with no continuity field would tell the session that no cross-plan ruling governs the project. Halting on a damaged file is loud, recoverable, and correct; quietly forgetting a governing rule is neither.

retrieval_boundary.trigger: a concrete question about a ruling named in the live projection, about a cold ruling, or an explicit operator request for prior-plan history
retrieval_boundary.grain: one ## Cold index section read, or one decision body, or one plan-ledger entry, per retrieval
retrieval_boundary.promotion: a retrieved cold body is never promoted back into the live index
retrieval_boundary.ledger_promise: For a row recorded by a ledger closeout the retrieval promise is the ruling, not the body — permanently, and regardless of what any later closeout chooses. No later archive+index closeout repairs an earlier ledger one.

publication.rule: Every publication this contract performs — the artifact, both reservation files, and the archive/INDEX.md row — goes through one commit-aware step that classifies its own result from what is on disk, against the bytes that were there before and the bytes being published. Nothing is keyed on "a refusal was raised".
publication.why: The shared atomic-write primitive commits a first publication with os.link and then unlinks its temporary name, so a named refusal can arrive after the commit. A marker rule keyed on the refusal would mark a recorded plan's reservation and let the release hand its id back.

residue.collapse_bound: inode identity, over the primitive's own fixed temp-name shape
collapse_points: after the publication, as part of classifying it
residue.post_commit_outcome: A published result whose residue collapsed — or that had none — is a successful pass: exit 0, the evidence close runs, and publication_residue_collapsed records which it was. continuity-publication-cleanup-failed names exactly one condition: published with at least one sibling still sharing the artifact's inode after the collapse.

reservation.purpose: A ledger closeout creates archive/PLAN-NNN/ containing NOT-ARCHIVED.md, no CLOSEOUT.md, and — only after an attempt proven not to have committed — LEDGER-FAILED.md. It holds no plan content: it occupies the plan id so no later closeout can reuse it, and it carries on disk, without reference to CONTINUITY.md, whether the attempt that created it recorded nothing.
reservation.index_row_rule: The summary is fixed text, so a reservation's row is self-identifying and a real archive's row is never a reservation row. Creation and adoption ensure the row strictly after the sentinel and strictly before publication is reachable, and no writer removes it while the sentinel survives — which is what makes a sentinel without its row a durable proof that nothing was committed.

shapes.meaning: a whole reservation whose last compute pass ended in a named refusal with publication outcome not-published
a release in progress; non-commit is still proven by the surviving marker
a creation interrupted between mkdir and its first file, or a release one step further on
a creation or adoption interrupted inside the binding step, between the sentinel and the index row — before anything could be committed
a whole reservation whose last attempt never said how it ended; whether the plan is recorded is undecidable from archive/ alone

reservation.occupies_id_in_every_shape: archive-plan's allocator and prompt_evidence.current_plan_id both match on PLAN-NNN directory names and never on their contents, so every shape occupies its id identically and no repair window can double-allocate.
reservation.not_continuity: Neither reservation file, nor the publication residue of either, is a continuity artifact under any reading: neither carries a row, a ledger section, or a Format header, and no reader parses either.

window_witness.definition: W(X) holds for a plan id X when prompt_evidence.read_ledger(root, plan_id=X) returns at least one admitted record and reports no foreign-plan-window error. At most one W(X) can hold.
silent_when: the log holds no admitted record
separates: a closeout that was abandoned and whose window has since closed
a later plan closing over an older reservation

evidence_close.rule: Every outcome closes its prompt-effectiveness window exactly once, against the plan that is closing.

owners.window: derived — correct, because nothing was allocated

evidence_close.ordering: after the continuity write, never before: it performs an irreversible delete, so a write that refuses must leave the log intact for the retry.

witness_rule.runs: close_plan_sequence — re-entrant, reads nothing, writes nothing

witness_rule.witness: W(Y) for some Y != P, or the log mixes windows

retention.rule: Closed plan-ledger entries and cold-index rows are never deleted automatically. Under ledger they are the only surviving record of that plan, and a background pruner would destroy information the operator explicitly chose to keep. Growth is bounded by a declared file ceiling instead.

scopes.effect: replace a closed plan's ledger section with a tombstone, preserving the heading, closed date, and preservation value verbatim
remove a cold-index row whose body survives elsewhere; Pruned increases by one so a session is never told a ruling never existed

preservation_rules.rule: a --cold row's Body must be a locator naming an existing file
no identity given to --cold may name a live row
every --plan must name a recorded, non-tombstoned section
no --plan may name the plan equal to Highest plan recorded
at least one --plan or --cold must be given

refusal_codes.meaning: the artifact is a symlink, a non-regular file, or a hardlink
the artifact is not valid UTF-8
the Format header is missing or names a format this reader does not implement
a required section or field is malformed; the detail names the section
a Scope or Ruling value read from decisions/ breaks the field grammar or a bound
a Supersedes or Expires value read from decisions/ breaks the reference grammar
a reference header carries more than eight references
a reference resolves to no live row, or a bare reference would reach a prior plan
a bare reference resolves to more than one row
a decision names itself
two or more decisions claim the same target with the same disposition
one target is named with conflicting dispositions
a locked decision carries Supersedes: but publishes no Scope/Ruling pair
a decision basename is not DEC-NNN.md
an archive+index row names a body file that does not exist under the archive it is bound to
an index-mode --plan does not name the real, highest, above-H archive that closeout just created
root IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md is absent, so a compute pass could be reading a decisions/ directory reset has already touched
--plan does not match the resolved plan id
--plan names a recorded plan below the highest recorded plan
a ledger-replace --mode disagrees with the recorded preservation value
a ledger-replace --closed disagrees with the recorded closed date
--mode ledger names a plan that has a real archive, so its outcome is archive+index
the witness is silent and --plan is required; the refusal states both remedies verbatim
a reservation exists and the witness cannot say whether this is a retry or a later plan; the refusal states both remedies verbatim
a compute pass would bind an id the window witness contradicts
no further plan id can be allocated at 999; nothing is created and nothing is written
archive/PLAN-NNN exists in any form where a reservation would be created
archive/PLAN-NNN is neither a reservation of any named shape nor a real archive
a complete, unmarked reservation cannot be released; the refusal names the one enabled-path remedy
LEDGER-FAILED.md names a plan other than --plan
--plan is not the highest-numbered archive entry while its directory still occupies its id
the prompt-evidence log names a window other than --plan
a reservation or index mutation was classified not-published
a reservation or index mutation settled neither question
a reservation or index publication committed but its residue survived the collapse
the artifact publication committed but at least one sibling still shares its inode after the collapse
the artifact publication was classified not-published and the primitive reported no rule of its own; the primitive's own refusal code is surfaced where it has one
the artifact holds neither the bytes the pass read nor the bytes it was publishing
the composed ledger section exceeds the declared section bound
the write would cross the file ceiling; the refusal names the prune that can still recover capacity
the ceiling is reached with every prunable byte already reclaimed; there is no further mediated recovery
a --cold row has no surviving archived body
--cold names a live row
--plan names no recorded, non-tombstoned section, or --cold names no cold row
--plan names the newest recorded plan

unchanged_surfaces.archive-plan: No change. Its allocator is unchanged, it reads no continuity artifact, and ARCHIVE_ROOT_FILES must not gain CONTINUITY.md. Its _index_body / _atomic_text helpers are reused for archive/INDEX.md, which is a call, not a change.
unchanged_surfaces.reset-plan: No change. Its allowlist must not gain CONTINUITY.md, archive/ must not become a reset target, and the ordering of RESET_ROOT_FILES before RESET_CLEAR_DIRS stays load-bearing for the plan-surface guard.
unchanged_surfaces.prompt_evidence: No change. close_plan_sequence already accepts plan_id; read_ledger already accepts one and already reports every foreign record, which is the whole of the window witness.
unchanged_surfaces.atomic_write: No change. The first-publication os.link + os.unlink shape and the expect_absent exclusivity it provides stay exactly as they are; the publication step wraps the primitive with a classifier rather than altering its commit discipline.
